title: How Much Does Responsive (RFPIO) Cost in 2026? Pricing, Features and Reviews
summary: Responsive (formerly RFPIO) starts at $10,000 a year. See what teams really pay in 2026, each edition, hidden fees, features, and user reviews.
body_markdown:
*This guide is published by*[Inventive AI](https://www.inventive.ai/) *, an AI-native RFP response platform and Responsive alternative. Pricing data comes from Responsive's own pricing page, third-party procurement data, and verified reviews, so you can make your own call.*


Responsive (Responsive.io, formerly RFPIO) publishes one price and keeps the rest behind a sales call. That makes it hard to budget, and it's why "Responsive pricing" and "RFPIO pricing" are some of the most searched questions about the platform.


**The short answer:** Responsive's entry plan, Emerging Edition, starts at $10,000 a year, and the Growth and Enterprise editions are quote-only. Across 133 purchases in[Vendr's procurement data](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/responsive) , the median contract is $14,750 a year, with contracts ranging from about $5,500 to $40,300.


## **Key takeaways**


- **Starting price:** Emerging Edition starts at $10,000 a year. Growth and Enterprise require a quote.
- **Pricing model:** A platform fee, plus user licenses, plus add-ons and services. Projects are unlimited on every edition.
- **Contract costs:** The median contract is about $14,750 a year, and implementation, support, and add-ons often push total cost 20% to 40% above the subscription.
- **Negotiation room:** Multi-year terms, volume, and competitive evaluations commonly cut 10% to 30% off initial quotes.


## **What is Responsive (formerly RFPIO)?**


Responsive is an RFP tool and proposal software platform that helps proposal, sales, and security teams answer RFPs, RFIs, DDQs, and security questionnaires from a central content management system. It was founded as RFPIO in 2015 in Beaverton, Oregon, and rebranded as Responsive in July 2023 to reflect a scope wider than RFPs. Responsive now calls its category[strategic response management](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/strategic-response-management-business-success) (SRM).


Responsive isn't AI-native. It was built as a library-first platform, and its generative AI was added on top of that architecture recently. Teams store approved answers, the AI suggests and drafts responses from that stored content, and contributors review and approve inside response projects. That design matters for accuracy: the AI can only be as current as the library behind it.


## **How does Responsive pricing work?**


Responsive prices every deployment on three components: an annual platform fee, user licenses, and add-ons and services. Response projects are unlimited on every edition, so RFP volume doesn't raise the bill, but the edition, the number of licensed users, and the extras you add do.


1. **Platform fee:** An annual subscription for the edition you choose (Emerging, Growth, or Enterprise). Every edition includes centralized content, collaboration workflows, AI-powered response support, and standard integrations.
2. **User licenses:** Licensed users are priced on top of the platform fee. Guest users are unlimited, so occasional reviewers can contribute without a full license.
3. **Add-ons and services:** Professional services, premium onboarding and support, LookUp, Trust Center, translation, and premium connectors are scoped separately.


Contracts are typically annual, and multi-year agreements of two to three years are common and often come with 10% to 20% discounts or price locks.

## **How much does each Responsive edition cost?**


Emerging Edition starts at $10,000 a year. Growth and Enterprise are quote-only, and contracts across all three range from roughly $5,500 to $40,300 a year, with a median of $14,750.


### **How much does Responsive Emerging Edition cost?**


Emerging starts at $10,000 a year, the only price Responsive publishes. It's built for teams setting up a structured RFP process for the first time and includes unlimited response projects, requirements analysis, Responsive AI agents, the content library, Ask, templates, standard reports, and an executive dashboard.


**Best for:** Early-stage proposal teams with low-to-moderate RFP volume.


### **How much does Responsive Growth Edition cost?**


Growth is quote-only. It adds intake requests, LookUp, eSignature, advanced integrations, advanced access controls, premium deployment and support, and flexible hosting options.


**Best for:** Teams handling weekly RFPs with cross-functional collaboration and CRM-driven workflows.


### **How much does Responsive Enterprise Edition cost?**


Enterprise is quote-only. It adds flexible custom AI, enterprise security and controls, advanced reporting, and premium connectors.


**Best for:** Dedicated proposal operations with legal, InfoSec, and compliance involvement across regions or business units.

## **What hidden costs come with Responsive?**


The subscription is usually only part of the bill. Per Vendr, total cost of ownership including implementation, support, and add-ons often runs 20% to 40% above the base subscription. Budget for:


- **Implementation and onboarding:** Setup, content migration, and training are quoted separately and often equal 20% to 40% of the first-year subscription.
- **Premium support or customer success:** Typically 10% to 20% of annual subscription value when it isn't included in your edition.
- **AI and automation add-ons:** AI Agent Studio and the newer AI agents are marked early access on Responsive's pricing page, along with TRACE Score, and Agent Studio limits (5, 10, or 20 agents) vary by edition, so confirm what yours includes.
- **Integrations and API access:** CRM connectors, premium connectors, and API access can carry setup or licensing fees, and some sit only in higher editions.
- **Extra products:** LookUp, Trust Center, content translation, business units, and sandboxes are separate line items.
- **User expansion:** Adding licensed users mid-contract can trigger higher per-seat rates or pro-rated charges.
- **Renewal increases:** Auto-renewal clauses with annual increases of 3% to 7% are common unless you negotiate a cap.


There's also the cost that never appears on a quote: keeping the content library accurate. Responsive's AI drafts from that library, so someone has to review, merge, and retire answers on a schedule, or response quality slips.

## **What features does Responsive AI offer for RFPs and sales enablement?**


Responsive combines a content library, response project workflows, and a[growing set of AI agents](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/rfp-ai-agents-explained) , with integrations and enterprise security on higher editions. For sales enablement, LookUp puts approved answers in front of reps inside the tools they already use.


- **Response projects and requirements analysis:** Unlimited projects for RFPs, RFIs, DDQs, and security questionnaires, with requirements extracted from incoming documents.
- **Content library and Ask:** A[central library of approved answers](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/building-competitive-rfp-answer-library) that teams search, reuse, and maintain, with SME assignments, collaborator recommendations, and review and approval steps inside each project.
- **Responsive AI:** AI-powered content generation, editing with pre-built prompts, collaborator recommendations, and smart search.
- **AI agents (early access):** Analysis, Executive Summary, Fit Analysis, and Omnichannel Answering agents, plus an AI Agent Studio capped at 5, 10, or 20 agents by edition. You can also bring your own OpenAI or Azure account.
- **TRACE Score (early access):** Launched in April 2025, it scores every AI-generated answer from 0 to 100 on trustworthiness, relevance, accuracy, completeness, and explainability.
- **Content Health Dashboard:** Measures the library's accuracy, freshness, duplication, and compliance, and recommends fixes for content owners to act on.
- **Intake, LookUp, and eSignature:** Request intake, on-demand content access for frontline sellers, and signatures, from Growth Edition up.
- **Integrations:** Connectors for CRM, cloud storage, collaboration tools, sales enablement platforms, and developer and support desk tools.
- **Security and administration:**[SOC 2 Type 2](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/soc-2-type-2) , SSO and SAML-based SSO, multi-factor authentication, 256-bit encryption, custom roles, data retention policies, and cloud hosting options including GovCloud.
- **Trust Center:** A separate product for sharing prefilled questionnaires and documents with customers and prospects.


## **What strengths do Responsive (RFPIO) reviews point to?**


Reviewers credit Responsive with strong collaboration across departments, a mature content library, and enterprise-grade security. It holds[4.5/5](https://www.g2.com/products/responsive-formerly-rfpio/reviews) on G2 across 1,313 reviews, 4.5/5 on Capterra across 190 reviews, and[4.3/5](https://www.gartner.com/reviews/market/rfp-response-management-applications/vendor/responsive/product/responsive) on Gartner Peer Insights. On G2, ease of use is the most-mentioned pro (340 mentions).


**What a Responsive user likes:** Alaina S., Proposal Manager (Enterprise), on G2: "It solves the headache of having hundreds of past proposals scattered in various inboxes, shared drives, and hard drives."


- **Cross-functional collaboration:** Configurable workflows route questions to sales, legal, security, and product reviewers inside one project.
- **Unlimited projects and guest users:** Volume doesn't raise the price, and occasional contributors don't need a full license.
- **Mature content library:** Centralized answers with tagging and search suit teams with established content programs.
- **Broad integrations:** CRM, cloud storage, collaboration, and sales enablement connectors fit large tech stacks.
- **Enterprise security and hosting:** SOC 2 Type 2, SAML SSO, customer-managed encryption keys, and GovCloud options suit regulated buyers.


## **What concerns do buyers raise about Responsive?**


The most common concerns are opaque pricing above the entry edition, search and customization limits, and AI quality that depends on how well the library is maintained. On G2, the most-mentioned cons are a steep learning curve (71 mentions) and an interface users find unintuitive (60).


- **Pricing beyond Emerging:** Only the $10,000 starting price is public, so Growth and Enterprise budgeting requires a sales cycle.
- **Inconsistent licensing:** Reviewers report Responsive has moved away from unlimited users and projects toward capped blocks of users and projects, leaving pricing inconsistent across accounts.
- **Search and customization:** Reviewers report slower search as the library grows and fewer options for tailoring workflows.
- **AI added to a library-first platform:** Responsive wasn't built AI-native, and its AI drafts from stored content, so outdated or conflicting entries carry into drafts unless someone keeps the library current.
- **Early-access AI:** TRACE Score, AI Agent Studio, and the Analysis, Executive Summary, Fit Analysis, and Omnichannel Answering agents are still marked early access on Responsive's pricing page.

*All reviews from Responsive's G2 reviews page.*


### **What implementation risks come with Responsive?**


The main risks are cost and time to value. Implementation, content migration, and training are quoted separately, and the AI produces useful drafts only after the library is populated and organized. Teams also need an owner to keep content current after launch, or answer quality drifts.


## **How can you negotiate a lower Responsive price?**


The biggest savings come from multi-year terms, volume, and a real competitive evaluation. Vendr's deal data points to these levers:


1. **Commit multi-year:** 2-3 year agreements often yield 10% to 20% discounts or price locks.
2. **Negotiate volume:** Larger deployments (25, 50, or 100+ users) commonly get 15% to 30% lower per-user pricing.
3. **Run a competitive evaluation:** Evaluating alternatives like Loopio or Qvidian often unlocks another 5% to 15%, or bundled implementation and support.
4. **Prepay annually:** Annual prepayment can save 5% to 10% compared to monthly billing.
5. **Cap renewals and start early:** Negotiate a 3% to 5% renewal cap upfront, and engage 60 to 90 days before renewal, ideally near quarter-end.


## **Does Responsive give the best value for money compared to other RFP response systems?**


Responsive is strong value for high-volume, multi-department teams and weaker value for small teams or teams without someone to maintain the library. Unlimited projects and guest users mean the cost per RFP keeps falling as volume grows: at the $14,750 median, 50 RFPs a year works out to about $295 each, and 150 RFPs to about $98.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### How does Responsive use AI to suggest answers and reduce duplication?


It matches each incoming question to the closest approved answers in the library and drafts from them, so teams reuse one vetted answer instead of writing new versions each time. Its Content Health Dashboard flags duplicate and stale entries, but content owners still merge and retire them, because the AI can only reuse what the library holds.


### Can Responsive work as an AI sales agent?


Partly. Two pieces serve sellers: LookUp gives reps on-demand access to approved RFP content inside the tools they already use, and the Omnichannel Answering Agent (early access) answers questions across channels. Both draw from the content library, so they're strongest on repeat questions and weakest on deal-specific context the library doesn't hold.


### Is Responsive's AI safe for governed enterprise use?


Its security controls are strong: SOC 2 Type 2, SAML SSO, custom roles, data retention policies, customer-managed encryption keys, and the option to bring your own OpenAI or Azure account. TRACE Score, still marked early access, adds a 0 to 100 quality rating on AI answers, but drafts are still only as current as the library behind them.


### What support options does Responsive offer?


Responsive's support options include help content, the Responsive Community, Responsive Academy, a standard support package with web-based ticketing, and standard data migration. Premium onboarding and a premium support package are available as paid upgrades, and Responsive also sells professional services from APMP-certified consultants.


### Should you choose Responsive or build in-house AI for RFPs?


In-house AI like ChatGPT or Claude costs less upfront but leaves you to build retrieval, permissions, review workflows, and answer tracking yourself, and answers stay only as accurate as the documents you feed it each time. Responsive gives you those workflows out of the box at $10,000+ a year. Our[Claude vs Responsive comparison](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/claude-vs-responsive-for-rfp-responses) walks through the trade-offs.


### Responsive or Qvidian: which is better for enterprise teams?


Both are library-first platforms with AI added later. Qvidian, part of Upland Software, leans on reporting depth and structured governance, while Responsive offers unlimited projects and guest users, broader collaboration workflows, and GovCloud hosting. Vendr data suggests Qvidian contracts typically start at a higher user minimum (10 to 15 users versus 5 to 10 for Responsive).


### Responsive or AutogenAI: which should proposal teams pick?


They solve different problems. AutogenAI generates original long-form narrative from your past proposals, which suits bid writers and government tenders. Responsive manages a content library and response workflows, which suits teams answering high volumes of structured RFPs and questionnaires. Teams that need both narrative drafting and question-by-question answers often evaluate an AI-native platform that covers each.


### Responsive or Dasseti Engage: which is better for RFP and DDQ automation?


Dasseti Engage is built mainly for asset managers answering DDQs, RFPs, and investor questionnaires, while Responsive is a cross-industry response platform. Investment firms focused on due diligence often prefer the specialist, and teams that also handle sales RFPs and security questionnaires across departments lean toward Responsive.


### Responsive or XaitPorter: what's the difference?


XaitPorter is a co-authoring tool for long, structured documents like bids and tenders, where many writers edit one document at the same time. Responsive is built around a Q&A content library and question-by-question response projects. Teams writing narrative bids lean toward XaitPorter, and teams answering high volumes of questionnaires lean toward Responsive.
